roadmap_item.title: Separate enduring capabilities from delivery changes
roadmap_item.description: Make feature dossiers distinguish enduring product capabilities from linked delivery changes, provisional findings, and known gaps.
roadmap_item.rationale: Cassor needs to preserve current product truth while allowing a capability to receive multiple independently verified changes over time.

goal: Cassor can maintain an enduring capability dossier with explicit linked changes, accepted state history, provisional findings, and projections that distinguish current truth from intended work.

included: Explicit Change-to-Capability links with validation and history
Append-only accepted capability state history sourced from verified changes
Attributed provisional and accepted dossier artifacts
Role-scoped and default context projections for capabilities, changes, and gaps
Roadmap projections for current truth, in-flight changes, planned work, and known gaps
Migration and portable export/import support for the new logical records
excluded: Runtime-specific worker adapters or benchmark work

decisions: The existing roadmap item feature types remain canonical: Capability, Change, and Gap.
A typed change_of link records a Change as belonging to a Capability; existing generic relationships remain supported.
Accepted capability state updates are append-only records and update current_state only through an explicit acceptance operation.
Provisional dossier artifacts are explicitly Draft and cannot affect execution authority, plan approval, completion, or canonical current state until accepted by the orchestrator.
Existing non-empty current_state values are preserved as accepted baseline history during migration without inventing a source change.

acceptance_criteria.title: One capability can receive multiple linked changes without losing prior delivery history.
CLI context and roadmap projections distinguish current product truth from proposed, in-flight, and completed changes.
Draft findings cannot become execution authority, accepted product truth, or completion evidence without explicit acceptance.
A completed change can be explicitly accepted as a capability update with traceable source and preserved history.
Existing databases migrate safely and the new dossier records remain deterministic across export and import.

constraints: SQLite remains the authoritative live state store.
Approved plan revisions, tasks, criteria, and evidence remain attached to delivery changes.
Historical state and accepted artifacts are never silently overwritten.
Generated roadmap files remain projections rather than import authorities.

tasks.title: Add capability-change and accepted-state schema
tasks.description: Add typed change links, append-only capability state history, attributed dossier artifacts, deterministic migration, and portable state support.

tasks.title: Implement dossier mutation and authority rules
tasks.description: Add store and CLI operations for linking changes, recording draft artifacts, accepting artifacts, and accepting verified capability state updates while keeping drafts outside execution authority.

tasks.title: Expose capability and change projections
tasks.description: Extend compact and scoped context plus the generated roadmap projection and views to show current capabilities, linked delivery changes, planned work, and known gaps.

tasks.title: Verify dossier evolution and document the model
tasks.description: Exercise one capability receiving two successive changes and a known gap, verify traceable accepted updates and draft isolation, and document the durable capability/change boundary.

risks: Existing generic feature relationships and non-empty current state need compatibility-preserving migration.
Adding dossier artifacts and state records expands the portable format and requires deterministic ordering.
The generated site may need focused view changes to make current truth and intended change unambiguous without duplicating the database model.
